chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Hilal from Ula'a ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a single revocable divorce while she was in a state of purity, then her husband died while she was in her waiting period. He said: 'She inherits him, then she observes the waiting period of the one whose husband died, and if she dies before the waiting period concludes from him, she inherits him and he inherits her.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: the one whose husband has died (widow)
key_terms.عَلَى طُهْرٍ: while in a state of purity (not menstruating)

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and waiting period rules for a divorced woman whose husband dies during her iddah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the legal status of a woman in a single revocable divorce (talaq raj'i) upon her husband's death, establishing that she transitions from a divorced wife to a widow for inheritance purposes. The hadith highlights the continuity of marital bonds during the waiting period (iddah), ensuring mutual inheritance rights regardless of whether the husband or wife dies first, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the finality of divorce versus death.
